sources.title: First National Communication to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
sources.organization: Republic of Equatorial Guinea, Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Forests and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate and institutional assessment published in 2019; some baselines cite the 2013 adaptation plan.
sources.methodology: National climate communication with sector analyses and proposed adaptation priorities.
sources.limitations: Institutional conditions and proposals are historical; manager-level water conflict is not armed conflict.

sources.title: Contribuciones Determinadas a Nivel Nacional (CDN), actualización 2022
sources.organization: Republic of Equatorial Guinea, Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Forests and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: 2022 update; vulnerability passages draw partly on 2013 and 2016 evidence; targets extend to 2050.
sources.methodology: Government NDC using climate-station trends and prior national assessments.
sources.limitations: Superseded by the NDC 3.0 registered in October 2026; cited station series are sparse and older.

sources.title: SCALA Equatorial Guinea
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme and Food and Agriculture Organization
sources.temporal_coverage: The page reports government engagement and meetings in September–October 2023; other project statistics are undated.
sources.methodology: UNDP project page describing national programme engagement and intended support.
sources.limitations: The page also contains stale NAP-status text; only dated 2023 activities are used.

sources.title: Equatorial Guinea Economic Update 2024: Designing Fiscal Instruments for Sustainable Forestry
sources.temporal_coverage: Second edition published June 2024; forestry status and institutional review are reported for that edition.
sources.methodology: Economic update combining forestry-sector review and fiscal-policy analysis.
sources.limitations: Recommended reforms are proposals, not evaluated adaptation outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: The communication says climate-driven temperature and rainfall changes will strongly affect water, alongside existing disputes among water managers over resource control and use; it proposes basin-level independent coordination.
claims.scenario: The communication does not specify a climate scenario.
claims.limitations: The reported dispute is administrative resource-use conflict, not armed violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The communication directly links climate effects on water with conflict among managers over control and use.

claims.paraphrase: The report says the absence of a national meteorological system prevents services for agriculture, fishing and water management, including early warnings for floods and dangerous weather.
claims.limitations: This describes the 2019 report's baseline and project proposal.

claims.paraphrase: The NDC relies on only two ASECNA stations, in Malabo and Bata; cited trends show significantly rising temperatures in Malabo but a different pattern in Bata, with no significant accumulated-rainfall trend.
claims.limitations: The series are sparse and cited from 2016; they do not support national extrapolation.

claims.locator: PDF p.18, vulnerability and reported climate changes.
claims.paraphrase: Citing the 2013 adaptation plan, the NDC reports that residents had noted more storms and floods, drying springs and warmer conditions; it labels the country highly vulnerable.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Forests and Environment
claims.limitations: The passage relays older 2013 observations, not a new survey.

claims.locator: PDF p.26, coastal and mangrove targets.
claims.paraphrase: The 2022 NDC sets targets for protecting 50% of the coast by 2050 and restoring 1,300 hectares and conserving 24,700 hectares of mangroves.
claims.limitations: These are targets in the superseded 2022 NDC, not completed results.

claims.paraphrase: The government requested SCALA support to strengthen private-sector participation in adaptation; follow-up discussions sought evidence for climate-resilient agriculture and value-chain work linked to the GCF program.
claims.limitations: The page reports a request and discussions, not completed support or impact.

claims.paraphrase: The World Bank reports that no national forestry inventory has been completed since 1992 and no forestry management plans have been formulated or implemented; the governing law also awaits update.
claims.limitations: The report identifies a governance gap; it does not measure climate adaptation outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF pp.12 and 57–58, funding and proposed forest measures.
claims.paraphrase: The report says funding for local and communal forests, indigenous populations, rural women and smallholders is inadequate; it recommends participatory forest management and benefit-sharing.
claims.limitations: The report's proposed measures are not assessed as implemented capacity.

access_audit.locator: Opened original 160-page national communication; cited PDF pp.136, 151.
access_audit.notes: Cover dates the communication 2019; water-manager conflict is not characterized as armed violence.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Government report permits educational partial reproduction with attribution; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Opened original 40-page Spanish NDC; cited PDF pp.18 and 26.
access_audit.notes: This 2022 version is not treated as current after the NDC 3.0 registry entry.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Opened project description and dated September–October 2023 activity passages.
access_audit.notes: Undated page has older NAP-status text; only dated activity statements are retained.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Opened original 64-page Economic Update; cited PDF pp.12 and 57–58.
access_audit.notes: Second edition cover dates the report June 2024; recommendations remain proposals.
access_audit.reuse_terms: World Bank permits attributed noncommercial reproduction; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Direct request timed out; UNFCCC registry record identifies NDC 3.0 as submitted 15 October 2026.
access_audit.notes: Registry metadata was used only to establish the newer version, not for substantive claims.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No claims derived from blocked PDF.

search_audit.query: Equatorial Guinea subnational climate vulnerability Malabo Bata coastal risk official assessment
search_audit.outcome: Opened the 2019 national communication and 2022 NDC; named-city station evidence is sparse and no recent municipal assessment was verified.

search_audit.query: Equatorial Guinea climate change conflict fragility water access social tensions primary report
search_audit.outcome: The 2019 communication links climate pressure on water with conflict among water managers; no armed-conflict or violence link was verified.

search_audit.query: Equatorial Guinea conflict insecurity forest management climate adaptation access constraints
search_audit.outcome: No primary source was found showing conflict or insecurity constraining climate adaptation; the forestry update discusses governance and participation constraints, not FCV violence.

search_audit.query: Equatorial Guinea adaptation capacity hydrometeorological services mangrove agriculture community forest official
search_audit.outcome: Government plans, dated UNDP engagement and World Bank forest-governance findings identify needs and proposed capacities; plans are not treated as outcomes.

gaps: The UNFCCC registry lists an Equatorial Guinea NDC 3.0 submitted on 15 October 2026, but direct PDF access timed out; the 2022 NDC is historical only.
No retrieved primary source substantiates climate-driven armed conflict or violence; the 2019 water-management passage concerns conflict among resource managers.
Recent municipality-level exposure data and evidence on insecurity obstructing adaptation were not verified; the cited climate-station analysis is sparse and dated.
